proof.text: Take the conservative family of compatible geometric points provided by [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation], using its common closed fibres for the two systems. By [lem-per-admissible-modification-system] the blowup index is filtered; restrict to the cofinal tail dominating $Y_I$. Write $H_J=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y_J,\bar t_J}$ and $H'_J=\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y'_J,\bar t'_J}$. For $J\le K$ the domination morphism $Y_K\to Y_J$ sends $\bar t_K$ to $\bar t_J$, and $Y'_J\to Y_J$ sends $\bar t'_J$ to $\bar t_J$ (the closed fibres are identified through these maps). Clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] gives a unique local homomorphism $H_J\to H_K$ (resp. $H_J\to H'_J$, $H'_J\to H'_K$) compatible with the structural maps and inducing the inclusion of the residue fields of clause (1) inside $\Omega$. A composite of two such maps is local and has both compatibilities, so by this uniqueness the maps form directed systems and commute with the maps $H_J\to H'_J$; clause (4) describes them on representative neighbourhoods $V\mapsto V\times_{Y_J}Y_K$. The rings $H_J,H'_J$ are strictly henselian by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-local-structure]. Thus [lem-sfb-filtered-colimit-strictly-henselian-local] gives henselian local colimits $B,B'$. By [lem-sfb-local-colimit-residue-field] their structure maps and the induced $u:B\to B'$ are local, and their maximal ideals are the unions of the stage maximal ideals. In particular $1\ne0$ in both colimits: it is already unequal at every local stage, and the residue-field colimit is a field. If the family is empty, all conclusions indexed by its points are vacuous.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373, local rings at geometric points of admissible-modification limits; explicit reconstruction of the reduction.

proof.text: On $Y_I$, [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] makes $I\mathcal O_{Y_I}$ an effective Cartier ideal. Choose an affine chart containing the marked point and an equation $\varphi$ there. Every later pointed local scheme maps into this chart, and its open complement of $V(I)$ is $D(\varphi)$. The density in [lem-per-admissible-modification-system], pulled back to affine pointed etale neighbourhoods (flat by [def-weil-etale-morphism]) by [lemma-nagata-dense-flat-pullback], implies injectivity of restriction to $D(\varphi)$: an element killed by $\varphi$ restricts to zero there and hence is zero. Passing through the neighbourhood colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit] preserves this injectivity: an equation $\varphi x=0$ holds at a common later neighbourhood, where cancellation applies. The same finite-representative argument in the blowup colimit proves that $\varphi$ is regular in $B$. It generates $IB$ and is a nonunit since every marked point lies over $V(I)$. On the corresponding chart of $Y'_I$ the equation is the image $\varphi'$ of $\varphi$ and generates $I\mathcal O_{Y'_I}$ there, hence $I\mathcal O_{Y'_J}$ on its inverse image in $Y'_J$. The density clause of [lem-per-admissible-modification-system] is stated over $A$ only, so argue directly: by [thm-nagata-blowup-principalizes-center] $JA'\mathcal O_{Y'_J}$ is locally generated by a nonzerodivisor $\psi$, and $J^M\subseteq I$ ($J$ finitely generated, $V(J)=V(I)$), so locally $\psi^M=c\varphi'$; $\varphi'x=0$ gives $\psi^Mx=0$, so $x=0$. Hence restriction to $D(\varphi')$ is injective, $U'$ is schematically dense in $Y'_J$, and flat etale base change keeps $\varphi'$ regular. The colimit argument above gives a regular nonunit $\varphi'$ in $B'$ generating $IB'$. Equality and cancellation in these ring colimits are justified by [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise], with the stage ring as its own module.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373, local rings at geometric points of admissible-modification limits; explicit reconstruction of the reduction.

proof.text: Let $K=(a_1,\ldots,a_r)\subset B$ contain $\varphi^n$, $n\ge1$. Choose $b_i$ with $\varphi^n=\sum b_i a_i$. The representative and eventual-zero clauses of [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise], first in the blowup colimit and then in the pointed etale colimit defining a strict henselization, place the finitely many $a_i,b_i$ and this equation on one affine pointed etale neighbourhood $V\to Y_J$. Shrink to the inverse image of the chosen exceptional chart. All these operations preserve the marked point. The ideal $(a_1,\ldots,a_r)$ on $V$ equals the unit ideal above $U$, since it contains $\varphi^n$ there. The schemes $Y_J$ are qcqs: [lemma-nagata-blowup-proper] makes them proper over the affine base. The chart argument of step 2 covers all of $Y_J$. Its complement of $U$ is the effective Cartier divisor locally given by $\varphi$, by the density/cancellation argument of step 2. Apply [lem-per-etale-supported-ideal-principalization] to $V\to Y_J$ and this ideal. It produces a $U$-admissible modification $W\to Y_J$ on whose pullback of $V$ the extended ideal is invertible.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373, local rings at geometric points of admissible-modification limits; explicit reconstruction of the reduction.

proof.text: By clause (1) of [lem-trf-module-admissible-blowup-calculus], the composite $W\to Y_J\to X$ is a blowup with finite-type centre supported on $V(J)$ union the image of the new centre, hence exactly $V(I)$. Thus $W$ is an index of our system. Its compatible geometric point lifts to the pulled-back pointed etale neighbourhood $V\times_{Y_J}W$. The ideal there has a local generator $a$, by [lem-per-etale-supported-ideal-principalization]; the pointed-neighbourhood colimit carries this generator and its finite expressions to $B$, so $K=(a)$. The equality $\varphi^n=ab$ survives in $B$. If $ax=0$, then $\varphi^n x=bax=0$ and step 2 gives $x=0$. Thus $a$ is a nonzerodivisor even though the transition maps between blowups need not be flat. This proves the required property for every finite ideal $K$, rather than merely for ideals extended from $A$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373, local rings at geometric points of admissible-modification limits; explicit reconstruction of the reduction.

proof.text: Repeat steps 3 and 4 for $B'$ and $\varphi'$, starting with any finite ideal containing $(\varphi')^n$. The complete system of blowups of $A'$ is allowed for this argument. The cofinality assertion in [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation] then identifies its colimit with the colimit over the corresponding blowups extended from $A$ used to define $B'$. Hence every such ideal is principal with a regular generator in precisely the ring occurring in the statement. This step needs no flatness of $A\to\widehat A$.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373, local rings at geometric points of admissible-modification limits; explicit reconstruction of the reduction.

proof.text: For a point $t$ of $\mathcal T$, its inverse image is a left adjoint, and so preserves colimits: applying the adjunction to maps from the proposed colimit into any set gives the same limit of Hom sets. Its composite with $p_J^{-1}$ is the stalk at $\bar t_J$, by compatibility of the point. The same assertion for abelian objects follows by carrying the addition and zero through these colimit maps. Consequently the definition of $L^q$ gives $(L^q_F)_t=\varinjlim_J(R^qj_{J*}F)_{\bar t_J}$, and the identical formula holds on the primed side. This is just the colimit universal property applied to the geometric-morphism adjunction of [def-trf-geometric-morphism] and the specified projections and points of [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation].

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373, local rings at geometric points of admissible-modification limits; explicit reconstruction of the reduction.

proof.text: The open immersion $j_J$ is qcqs: $U$ is the union of finitely many basic opens from generators of $I$, and $Y_J$ is separated over the affine base. Apply [prop-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-stalk-formula] to obtain canonical restriction isomorphisms $(R^qj_{J*}F)_{\bar t_J}\simeq H^q(U\times_{Y_J}\operatorname{Spec}H_J,F|)$. On the tail of step 2 these schemes are $\operatorname{Spec}H_J[1/\varphi]$, so they are affine and all transitions are affine. Their inverse limit is $\operatorname{Spec}B[1/\varphi]$: a ring map from the localization is exactly a compatible family of ring maps from the $H_J$ making $\varphi$ invertible. The sheaves are pullbacks of the one fixed sheaf $F$; they remain torsion by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-torsion]. Thus [lemma-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology-continuity] identifies the colimit in step 6 with $H^q(\operatorname{Spec}B[1/\varphi],F_t)$. The same argument gives the primed isomorphism. All comparison legs are restrictions; the construction works for every $q\ge0$ with the same rings and points.

source.place: XX 4.4, printed p.373, local rings at geometric points of admissible-modification limits; explicit reconstruction of the reduction.

proof.text: Finally check the arrow, before passing to any limit. On a pointed etale neighbourhood $V$ at $\bar t_J$ and its pulled-back neighbourhood on $Y'_J$, [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange] sends a section over $U\times_{Y_J}V$ to its restriction on the primed fibre product. For a chosen bounded-below injective resolution of $F$, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise] computes higher exchange by exactly these maps term by term, followed by comparison with an injective resolution on the primed side. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] identifies that composite on cohomology with the canonical pullback. The strict-local stalk maps of step 7 are the canonical restrictions of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-restriction]; by [lem-weil-pbc-strict-local-mate-continuity-presentation] the neighbourhood germs of classes on $U\times_{Y_J}V$ form a colimiting cocone and each germ followed by that map is the pullback to $U\times_{Y_J}\operatorname{Spec}H_J$. Thus their squares commute at each blowup index. Taking colimits of those commuting squares preserves equality: precomposing with every colimit leg gives the same map. The two composites at the final limit are restrictions along $\operatorname{Spec}B'[1/\varphi']\to\operatorname{Spec}B[1/\varphi]$, since $u(\varphi)=\varphi'$. The composition clause (4) of the same pullback lemma identifies their composite with that single pullback. The same check, for the domination maps $Y_K\to Y_J$ in place of $Y'_J\to Y_J$, shows that the transition maps of $L^q_F$ used in step 6 correspond under step 7 to the pullbacks along $\operatorname{Spec}H_K[1/\varphi]\to\operatorname{Spec}H_J[1/\varphi]$, as step 7 requires. This proves the asserted identification of the exchange map and also naturality in $F$.

title: Henselian valuative local rings and punctured-local stalk calculation
statement:
Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair with $I$ finitely generated, let $A'=\widehat A$ be its $I$-adic completion, and put $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $U=X\setminus V(I)$ and $U'=\operatorname{Spec}A'\times_XU$ [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. For each finitely generated ideal $J$ with $V(J)=V(I)$ write $Y_J=\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)$, and write $Y'_J$ for the corresponding blowup over $A'$ [def-nagata-affine-blowup]. Let $\mathcal T$ and $L^q_F,L^q_{F'}$ be the limit topos and colimit sheaves of [lem-per-admissible-modification-cohomology-presentation], for a torsion abelian etale sheaf $F$ on $U$ and its inverse image $F'$ on $U'$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves, def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. There is a conservative family of compatible geometric points $t=(\bar t_J)$ of the closed fibres for which the following holds. Form
$$B_t=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y_J,\bar t_J},\qquad B'_t=\varinjlim_J\mathcal O^{\mathrm{sh}}_{Y'_J,\bar t'_J}$$
using the compatible points on corresponding closed fibres and strict henselizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. These are nonzero henselian local rings, with the induced local map $u_t:B_t\to B'_t$. There is a nonunit nonzerodivisor $\varphi_t\in B_t$ such that $IB_t=(\varphi_t)$ and $IB'_t=(\varphi'_t)$ for $\varphi'_t=u_t(\varphi_t)$, also a nonunit nonzerodivisor. In each ring every finitely generated ideal containing a positive power of its displayed principal ideal is principal and generated by a nonzerodivisor; this is the $I$-valuative property used here. Put $S_t=B_t[1/\varphi_t]$, $S'_t=B'_t[1/\varphi'_t]$, and let $F_t$ be the inverse image of $F$ under $\operatorname{Spec}S_t\to U$, with $F'_t$ its inverse image on $\operatorname{Spec}S'_t$. There are canonical restriction isomorphisms, for every $q\geq0$,
$$(L^q_F)_t\simeq H^q((\operatorname{Spec}S_t)_{\mathrm{et}},F_t),\qquad (L^q_{F'})_t\simeq H^q((\operatorname{Spec}S'_t)_{\mathrm{et}},F'_t).$$
Under these isomorphisms the exchange morphism on stalks is the pullback induced by $S_t\to S'_t$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback].
